chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Musawi narrated to me from 'Abdullah ibn Nuhayk, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you have finished your supplication by the grave, go to the pulpit, rub it with your hand, and hold its two knobs (rummanatayhi), which are the lower ones. Rub your face and eyes with them, for it is said that they are a cure for the eyes. Stand by it, praise Allah, glorify Him, and ask for your needs. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Between my pulpit and my grave [my house] is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And my pulpit is upon an oasis from the oases of Paradise, and the pillars of the pulpit are ranks in Paradise, and the oasis is the small door.' Then go to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and pray there as long as you wish. When you enter the mosque, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and when you leave, do the same, and increase your prayers in the mosque of the Prophet (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals and virtues associated with visiting the Prophet's pulpit and grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) details the ritual etiquette for visiting the Prophet's grave, emphasizing the spiritual merit of the space between the pulpit and the grave as a 'garden of Paradise' and instructing visitors to rub the minbar's knobs on their face for healing. This practice highlights the Shia belief in the physical sanctity of the Prophet's furnishings and the continuity of his presence, encouraging abundant salawat as a means of connecting with the Ahl al-Bayt.
